title: Choose the game world for Club Duel
question: The roll assigned Two-Player Cabinet. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Each sketch shows the admin console on its Courts tab: score race pinned on top, tabs below it.

options.label: Two-Player Cabinet
options.lineage: arcade cabinet attract screens and high-score tables, at modern resolution
options.thesis: The duel as a two-player cabinet: 1P and 2P counters up top, rounds called like stages, the ranking kept as the high-score table.
materials: flat marquee colour on a violet cabinet ground
options.viewport: 1P/2P band with rolling counters and twin power bars meeting at the midline; tabs; court cards with monumental court numbers, live pairs and End match.
options.risk: Arcade slides into retro costume (pixels, CRT glow) if it isn't kept crisp and flat; your 'modern' rules both out.

raised.raise: Court numbers go monumental and each court says one thing: what is on now, or what is next.
End tournament, Regenerate link and Remove sit apart from other buttons, outline-only until focused.
Lime means LIVE and nothing else, on every screen.
Nothing labelled twice: the side colour names the club, so pair labels drop the club prefix.
The high-score table runs at data density: one tabular face, aligned columns, no row chrome.

options.label: Captain's Draft
options.lineage: MOBA captain's-mode draft screens, where two captains fill picks down opposite sides
options.thesis: Captain's Mode is a draft: two captains fill slots down facing columns, and picks stay sealed until the match flips them.
options.viewport: Team totals bar across the top; tabs; each court a face-off of two slot frames across a centre spine, sealed slots in gold until the match starts.
options.risk: Familiar: dark esports drafting is where most game-UI runs land, and it tips into neon-glow cliché easily.

options.label: Console Home Rows
options.lineage: console home screens and streaming walls: rows of tiles where the focused one grows
options.thesis: Every tab is a wall of tile rows; the live match is the focused tile, grown and lit while the rest dim.
options.viewport: Totals hero tile split by club; tabs; a Courts row with live courts grown, then a Round 2 row of match tiles, pending ones as tile backs.
options.case: Wins identification (the console home screen gamers know by heart); loses clarity because rails hide matches past the phone's edge.
options.risk: Horizontal rails hide matches off-screen; the admin needs every court at once, so rows must wrap on the laptop.

options.label: Terminal Wayfinding
options.thesis: Courts signed like gates: one yellow band says which match plays where.
options.viewport: A yellow band per court with a monumental court number.
options.case: Clear for finding a court, but nothing in it reads as a game: loses identification, only ties clarity.
options.kept: Monumental court numbers, one message per court.
options.risk: Reads as an airport, not a game.

options.label: Graphite Console
options.thesis: Graphite panels split by hairline seams, destructive actions isolated.
options.viewport: Persistent tiled panels for courts, lineups and results.
options.case: Tidy for the admin, but a developer tool, not a game; loses identification and ties clarity.
options.kept: Destructive actions isolated and outline-only until focused.

options.label: Orienteering Map
options.thesis: Rounds as a purple course over a fixed terrain of courts.
options.viewport: Courts as terrain, the active round as the purple leg.
options.case: No game read and the map metaphor obscures scores; loses both axes.
options.kept: One reserved colour for the active state.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Every match a catalog number on matte black, names in colour code.
options.viewport: One pulse plot of the score history owning the screen.
options.case: Coded labels fight a glance-and-go scoreboard; loses both axes.
options.risk: Players can't read who is playing.

options.label: Datamatics
options.thesis: Scores as strobing black-and-white barcode columns.
options.viewport: Ranking as a dense monospace data field.
options.case: No club colour and no game read; loses both axes.
options.kept: Data-density tables in one tabular face.
options.risk: Strobing is hostile at a venue.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean sports-scores app, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Scoreboard header with both totals, segmented tabs, court cards in a clean grid.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every scores app; safe, not game-like.
